chapter.title: Routines
chapter.para: python.cls defines five public routines, the same as methods of &py;, named as BSF4ooRexx's bsf.import, box and bsf.redirectTo, for programs that prefer that style.

section.title: py.import
section.para: The same as : returns the module name.

example.title: py.import and py.kw
example.programlisting:
textwrap = py.import("textwrap") say textwrap~shorten("The quick brown fox jumps", py.kw("width", 15))
::requires "python.cls"

section.title: py.box
section.para: The same as : value as a Python object of the given type.

section.title: py.kw
section.para: The same as : keyword arguments, for the last argument of a call.

section.title: py.extend
section.para: Makes the Rexx class extend the Python class base, and returns the Python class it makes. class must be a subclass of PyObject. base is a Python class (a PyObject), a dotted name ("http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler"; a name without dots is a builtin, such as "str"), or a Rexx Array of them, for several bases. See .

section.title: py.redirectTo
section.para: Sends Rexx's standard streams to Python's, or back, with the arguments of BSF4ooRexx's bsf.redirectTo:

listitem.para: Python: .input reads sys.stdin; .output writes to sys.stdout; .error to sys.stderr; .debugInput and .traceOutput go with .input and .error, with their own prefixes. The other arguments, when given, replace each of them: a Python file object, or a PyInputStream or PyOutputStream, used as it is.
Rexx: back to Rexx's own .stdin, .stdout and .stderr.

section.para: prefixes is &true; (the default: BSF4ooRexx's prefixes, REXXin?>, REXXout>, REXXerr>, REXXdbgIn?> and REXXtrc>), &false; (none), or a Directory or StringTable from INPUT, OUTPUT, ERROR, DEBUGINPUT and TRACEOUTPUT to a prefix, &nil; for none; the streams it does not name have none. See .
